![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The current implementation only collects nodes present in the `players` dictionary. However, nodes that are already being despawned (e.g., via `despawn_eliminated_player`) are removed from this dictionary but remain in the scene tree for two frames. If `spawn_round_players` is called during this window, it will encounter name collisions because the old nodes are still in the container. 

Additionally, the helpful comment regarding `_connected_peers` was removed and should be restored for maintainability.

```
	var nodes_to_free: Array = _players_container.get_children()
	players.clear()
	# NOTE: _connected_peers is intentionally NOT cleared here;
	# connection state survives round transitions.
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The `prepare_for_despawn` method is missing from `scenes/characters/player.gd` (used for the Boss). While the `has_method` check prevents a crash, the Boss node will not be properly hidden or frozen during the two-frame transition period, which may lead to visual artifacts or physics interactions after the round ends.

## Code Review

This pull request introduces an asynchronous player cleanup process via clear_players_for_replacement to ensure nodes are properly despawned before a new round begins. Feedback focuses on preventing name collisions by iterating over all container children instead of just the players dictionary and using remove_child() before queue_free() to ensure immediate name availability for multiplayer synchronization. Additionally, the Boss character needs to implement prepare_for_despawn to avoid artifacts during the transition, and a previously removed comment regarding _connected_peers should be restored for maintainability.
